CLINICAL FEATURES OF ONCHOCERCIASIS (RIVER BLINDNESS)
Clinical Features
- Skin lesions, which may be localized or cover large areas
- Intense pruritus a cardinal symptom; may occur in the absence of the skin
lesions
- Dermatitis
- Skin eventually becomes lichenified from chronic scratching
- Post inflammatory confetti-like depigmentation on the skin ("leopard
skin") may occur in late onchodermatitis
- Onchocercomata
- Subcutaneous nodules which develop on various sites of the body and
contain myriad adult worms which can live for up to 14 years.
- Firm, non-tender lymphadenopathy is a common finding in patients with
chronically infected onchocerciasis
- "Hanging groin" describes the pendulous loose, atrophic skin sac that
contains these large nodes
- Microfilariae in the eye may lead to visual impairment and blindness
